selection_policy: Strategy-blind: selection uses only structural coverage dimensions (era, schema variant, object size, stream volume, stream life-stage, disconnected/crisis-adjacent context). Selection never used return, momentum, funding signal, factor result, future performance, PnL, or replication result. Rationale below was recorded before any Parser A vs Parser B comparison was run.

network_acquisition_decision.why: experiments/data/r1_ingest_contract.json:raw_store names a licensed Tardis vendor path ('/var/lib/qntylab/licensed/tardis/bybit-r1-v1', git_policy: never store vendor raw in git, retention: subject to vendor license); experiments/data/r1_data_source_qualification.json:decision is R1_DATA_SOURCE_QUALIFIED_PENDING_PROCUREMENT with metadata_endpoint_without_key=401. No Tardis API credential is present in this repository (verified: no TARDIS/API_KEY reference in qntylab/*.py). Rather than perform a new licensed-vendor download under ambiguous entitlement, this corpus reuses raw objects already legitimately present in .r1_input_cache/sha256/ (retrieved by an earlier, separate task) plus locally-authored synthetic fixtures.
network_acquisition_decision.consequence: MONUSDT, FHEUSDT, and a SANDUSDT-2024-11-04-vicinity object requested by the task brief's wishlist are NOT represented by real data in this corpus. 2023/2024/2025 eras are not represented by real data either. This is recorded as an explicit, known gap, not silently glossed over.

real_objects.why_selected: earliest available era (2020); major/high-liquidity instrument (BTCUSDT); establishes a baseline known_valid schema_variant=bybit_trade_v1 object with no observed anomalies
2021 era coverage; mid-size object; mid-volume stream
2022 era coverage; instrument later delisted (Anchor Protocol depeg, May 2022) giving a lifecycle-adjacent but pre-crisis snapshot; higher-volume stream than the 2020/2021 objects

disconnected/crisis-adjacent context: date falls within the FTX exchange collapse week (FTX halted withdrawals 2022-11-08); largest and highest-row-count object in the corpus, stress-testing parser throughput and dedup on a volatile, high-churn stream

known RPI schema_variant=bybit_trade_v1_rpi real-world instance (previously undercounted -- the frozen schema registry cites only a single 2026-06-30 DOLOUSDT RPI observation; this is a second, independent real RPI object); newest/near-cutoff era; smallest object and lowest-volume stream in the corpus; early-life instrument (recently listed meme perpetual)

synthetic_objects_location: tests/test_r1_reference_parser.py (each fixture is generated inline, in-memory, not persisted as a separate data file -- fixtures are small enough that the test source is the canonical record of their bytes)
not_yet_covered_by_this_corpus: truncated_csv (mid-row cutoff without trailing newline) -- exercised structurally via the truncated_tail_detected diagnostic path, but not asserted in a dedicated adversarial test in this pass
a real symbol-reuse (identity ambiguity) case -- out of scope for the trade-level parser under test; belongs to the lifecycle compiler
